subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should OpenClaw expose inbound WhatsApp call activity at all, and if so, should it be ephemeral plugin-hook data, a bounded agent-visible activity surface, or persisted contact-history state?
rationale: The implementation crosses user-activity privacy, authorization, retention, and public plugin/event-contract boundaries; source evidence confirms the transport event exists but cannot choose the permanent product semantics safely.

options.title: Approve a minimal ephemeral event
options.body: Add a default-off account-scoped WhatsApp call event with sanitized metadata and no contact-history persistence.

options.title: Design durable contact activity
options.body: First define retention, identity mapping, deletion, and agent-session semantics before storing calls as relationship history.

options.title: Decline inbound call exposure
options.body: Keep the existing outbound requester-bound call capability only and document that inbound call tracking is intentionally unsupported.

recommendation.title: Approve a minimal ephemeral event
recommendation.body: Add a default-off account-scoped WhatsApp call event with sanitized metadata and no contact-history persistence.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior issue comments and WhatsApp-plugin history provide the strongest direct evidence of ownership for this channel contract.
